label: Stars in the observable universe
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 23 zeros.
editorial_note: The observable universe holds an almost unimaginable sea of stars.

label: Grains of sand on Earth’s beaches
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 19 zeros.
editorial_note: All the world’s beaches still fall several scales short of the stars.

label: Microbes in a human body
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of trillions to hundreds of trillions.
editorial_note: A human body carries tens of trillions of microbes.

label: Insects alive on Earth
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 18 zeros.
editorial_note: Insects outnumber birds by millions to one.

label: Wild birds alive on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of billions to hundreds of billions.
editorial_note: Wild birds number in the tens of billions.

label: People alive on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from billions to tens of billions.
editorial_note: Humanity numbers in the billions.

label: Wild fish in the oceans
range_explanation: Estimates range from trillions to tens of trillions.
editorial_note: Ocean fish are thought to number in the trillions.

label: Trees on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from trillions to tens of trillions.
editorial_note: Earth has trillions of trees.

label: Stars your eyes can see in a dark sky
range_explanation: Estimates range from thousands to tens of thousands.
editorial_note: Only a few thousand stars are visible to unaided eyes at once.

label: Cells in one human body
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of trillions to hundreds of trillions.
editorial_note: A human body contains tens of trillions of cells.

label: Hairs on a full head of hair
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands.
editorial_note: A full head has roughly a hundred thousand hairs.

label: Drops of water in a bathtub
range_explanation: Estimates range from millions to tens of millions.
editorial_note: A bathtub holds millions of drops.

label: Grains of rice in a cereal bowl
range_explanation: A reasonable range stays around thousands.
editorial_note: A cereal bowl holds a few thousand grains of rice.

label: Ping-pong balls filling a swimming pool
range_explanation: Estimates range from millions to tens of millions.
editorial_note: A pool would take millions of ping-pong balls.

label: Marbles filling a school backpack
range_explanation: Estimates range from thousands to tens of thousands.
editorial_note: A backpack holds thousands of marbles.

label: Bricks in a brick house
range_explanation: A reasonable range stays around tens of thousands.
editorial_note: A brick house uses tens of thousands of bricks.

label: Ants alive on Earth
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 16 zeros.
editorial_note: Earth’s ants number in the tens of quadrillions.

label: Microbes in Earth’s oceans
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 29 zeros.
editorial_note: The oceans contain an enormous, mostly invisible living world.

label: LEGO bricks ever made
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of billions to trillions.
editorial_note: Hundreds of billions of LEGO pieces have been produced.

label: Cars on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from billions to tens of billions.
editorial_note: The world has around a billion cars.

label: Domesticated chickens alive on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of billions to hundreds of billions.
editorial_note: Chickens number in the tens of billions.

label: Golf balls that fit inside a Boeing 747
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of millions to hundreds of millions.
editorial_note: A Boeing 747 could hold tens of millions of golf balls by volume.

label: Tiny scales on a butterfly’s wings
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of thousands to tens of millions.
editorial_note: Butterfly wings are covered by hundreds of thousands to millions of scales.

label: An acorn growing into a full-sized oak
range_explanation: Estimates range from decades to centuries.
editorial_note: Growing a great oak takes decades.

label: A caterpillar changing into a butterfly
range_explanation: Estimates range from days to weeks.
editorial_note: The transformation takes days or weeks.

label: A snail crossing the United States
range_explanation: Estimates range from decades to centuries.
editorial_note: At a snail’s pace, the trip would take many decades.

label: A giant tortoise’s life
range_explanation: Estimates range from decades to centuries.
editorial_note: A giant tortoise can live for more than a century.

label: A mayfly’s adult life
range_explanation: Estimates range from minutes to days.
editorial_note: Many adult mayflies live only hours or days.

label: A spacecraft traveling to Mars
range_explanation: Estimates range from months to years.
editorial_note: A Mars journey usually takes many months.

label: An airplane flying around Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from days to weeks.
editorial_note: A round-the-world flight takes days.

label: A natural diamond forming underground
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of millions of years to billions of years.
editorial_note: Natural diamonds form over immense stretches of geological time.

label: An oyster growing a pearl
range_explanation: Estimates range from months to years.
editorial_note: A pearl can grow in months or a few years.

label: An oak tree’s life
range_explanation: A reasonable range stays around centuries.
editorial_note: Many oaks live for centuries.

label: A house cat’s life
range_explanation: Estimates range from years to decades.
editorial_note: A cat usually lives for years or decades.

label: A periodical cicada waiting underground
range_explanation: Estimates range from years to decades.
editorial_note: Some cicadas wait thirteen or seventeen years.

label: An adult butterfly’s life
range_explanation: Estimates range from weeks to months.
editorial_note: Many adult butterflies live only weeks.

label: An elephant pregnancy
range_explanation: Estimates range from months to years.
editorial_note: An elephant pregnancy lasts close to two years.

label: A sandcastle washing away
range_explanation: Estimates range from minutes to days.
editorial_note: A tide can erase a sandcastle in minutes or hours.

label: All the ants on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of billions of kilograms to trillions of kilograms.
editorial_note: Together, Earth’s ants weigh tens of billions of kilograms.

label: All the blue whales on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from billions of kilograms to tens of billions of kilograms.
editorial_note: Blue whales are huge, but there are relatively few of them.

label: All domesticated chickens
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of billions of kilograms to hundreds of billions of kilograms.
editorial_note: Billions of farmed chickens add up to an enormous mass.

label: All people on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of billions of kilograms to trillions of kilograms.
editorial_note: Billions of people together weigh hundreds of billions of kilograms.

label: All the water in Earth’s oceans
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 21 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: The oceans contain most of Earth’s surface water.

label: All the air in Earth’s atmosphere
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 18 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: The atmosphere is vast but far lighter than the oceans.

label: The ice covering Antarctica
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 19 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: Antarctica holds a continent-sized ice sheet.

label: All the buildings in New York City
range_explanation: Estimates range from trillions of kilograms to tens of trillions of kilograms.
editorial_note: A whole city is massive, but still far lighter than Everest.

label: The Moon
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 22 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: The Moon is a world made of rock.

label: Earth
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 24 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: Earth is much larger and denser than its moon.

label: The Sun
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 30 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: The Sun contains almost all the mass in our solar system.

label: All eight planets together
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 27 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: Even every planet together is tiny beside the Sun.

label: All cars on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from trillions of kilograms to tens of trillions of kilograms.
editorial_note: More than a billion heavy cars add up quickly.

label: All bicycles on Earth
range_explanation: Estimates range from tens of billions of kilograms to hundreds of billions of kilograms.
editorial_note: Bicycles are numerous but much lighter than cars.

label: One year’s world rice harvest
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of billions of kilograms to trillions of kilograms.
editorial_note: The world harvests hundreds of billions of kilograms of rice.

label: All the gold ever mined
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of millions of kilograms to billions of kilograms.
editorial_note: All mined gold would fit into a surprisingly small cube.

label: All whales alive today
range_explanation: Estimates range from billions of kilograms to hundreds of billions of kilograms.
editorial_note: Whales are huge, but their total mass is much smaller.

label: A school bus
range_explanation: A reasonable range stays around tens of thousands of kilograms.
editorial_note: A school bus weighs many thousands of kilograms.

label: An adult elephant
range_explanation: A reasonable range stays around thousands of kilograms.
editorial_note: A large elephant weighs several thousand kilograms.

label: A loaded cargo ship
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of millions of kilograms to billions of kilograms.
editorial_note: A cargo ship carries hundreds of millions of kilograms.

label: A blue whale
range_explanation: Estimates range from hundreds of thousands of kilograms to millions of kilograms.
editorial_note: A blue whale weighs hundreds of thousands of kilograms.

label: The water in all five Great Lakes
range_explanation: That is roughly a 1 followed by 16 zeros, measured in kilograms.
editorial_note: Together, the five Great Lakes hold about twenty quadrillion kilograms of freshwater.

label: Two mosquito wingbeats
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 300 to 600 wingbeats per second.
editorial_note: A mosquito’s wings move too quickly to follow with your eyes.

label: Two butterfly wingbeats
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 5 to 10 wingbeats per second.
editorial_note: A butterfly’s slower flaps are easy to see.

label: Two hummingbird wingbeats
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 40 to 80 wingbeats per second.
editorial_note: A hummingbird’s wings still move fast enough to blur.

label: Two hummingbird heartbeats
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 15 to 20 heartbeats per second.
editorial_note: A hummingbird has one of the fastest hearts among animals.

label: Two blue whale heartbeats
range_explanation: It takes about 5 to 20 seconds for one to happen.
editorial_note: A diving blue whale can slow its enormous heart dramatically.

label: Two shakes of a rattlesnake’s rattle
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 40 to 60 shakes per second.
editorial_note: A rattlesnake shakes its tail fast enough to make a continuous buzz.

label: A round-the-world cruise
range_explanation: A reasonable range stays around months.
editorial_note: A round-the-world cruise usually takes several months, with lots of stops along the way.

label: The Amazon River
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 6,400 to 6,800 kilometers.
editorial_note: River lengths depend on where their source is measured; estimates for the Amazon are usually about 6,400 to 6,800 kilometers.

label: The distance from Earth to the Sun
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 150 million kilometers.
editorial_note: Earth is about 150 million kilometers from the Sun on average.

label: The deepest borehole humans have drilled
range_explanation: A useful estimate is a little over 12 kilometers.
editorial_note: The Kola Superdeep Borehole reaches a little over 12 kilometers straight down into Earth.

label: A blue whale from nose to tail
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 25 to 33 meters.
editorial_note: A blue whale can grow to about 30 meters long—the length of a small row of cars.

label: The distance from Earth to the Moon
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 363,000 to 406,000 kilometers.
editorial_note: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometers away, and its oval path brings it a little nearer and farther each month.

label: The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park
order_of_magnitude: hundreds of thousands of square kilometers
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 344,000 square kilometers.
editorial_note: The Marine Park gives this comparison a clear official boundary.

label: The Sahara Desert
range_explanation: A useful estimate is roughly 8.5 to 10.5 million square kilometers.
editorial_note: The Sahara’s edge shifts, so its area needs a broad range.

label: The Pacific Ocean
order_of_magnitude: hundreds of millions of square kilometers
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 155 to 170 million square kilometers.
editorial_note: The Pacific covers more area than all of Earth’s land combined.

label: The water in Lake Erie
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 450 to 550 cubic kilometers of water.
editorial_note: Lake Erie is the shallowest Great Lake but still holds an enormous amount of water.

label: The water in all five Great Lakes
order_of_magnitude: tens of thousands of cubic kilometers
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 21,000 to 25,000 cubic kilometers of water.
editorial_note: Together, the five Great Lakes hold about 23,000 cubic kilometers of freshwater.

label: The water in all of Earth’s oceans
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 1.3 billion cubic kilometers of water.
editorial_note: Earth’s oceans hold about 1.3 billion cubic kilometers of water.

label: The line a BIC Cristal pen can write before it runs out of ink
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 2 to 3 kilometers.
editorial_note: Writing style changes the result, but a BIC Cristal is designed to draw at least two kilometers of line.

label: The silk thread in one silkworm cocoon
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 500 to 1,500 meters.
editorial_note: A silkworm wraps one remarkably long, continuous filament around itself.

label: The DNA in one human cell with a nucleus, stretched end to end
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 2 meters.
editorial_note: Nearly two meters of DNA fits inside a nucleus too small to see without a microscope.

label: The folded inside surface of an adult small intestine
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 25 to 35 square meters.
editorial_note: Tiny folds called villi and microvilli create far more food-absorbing surface than the intestine appears to have.

label: The gas-exchange surface inside a healthy adult’s lungs
range_explanation: A useful estimate is roughly 70 to 120 square meters.
editorial_note: Millions of tiny air sacs give adult lungs a surprisingly broad surface for exchanging gases.

label: The outer surface of an adult’s body
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 1.5 to 2 square meters.
editorial_note: Body size changes the answer, but an adult’s skin usually covers less area than a small bedsheet.

label: All the water floating in Earth’s atmosphere
order_of_magnitude: tens of thousands of cubic kilometers
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 12,900 cubic kilometers of water.
editorial_note: This includes invisible water vapor as well as the droplets and ice in clouds.

label: The blood one heart pumps in a day
range_explanation: A useful estimate is roughly 5,000 to 10,000 liters.
editorial_note: A heart keeps moving the same blood around the body, pumping thousands of liters in one day.

label: All the red blood cells in one adult, spread flat
range_explanation: A useful estimate is roughly 2,000 to 4,000 square meters.
editorial_note: Trillions of tiny red blood cells add up to a membrane surface measured in thousands of square meters.

label: A tectonic plate sliding across Earth
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 1 to 15 centimeters per year.
editorial_note: Different plates move at different rates, but their steady motion is measured in centimeters per year.

label: A healthy fingernail growing
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 2 to 5 millimeters per month.
editorial_note: Fingers and people differ, but healthy fingernails usually grow only a few millimeters each month.

label: Hair on a healthy scalp growing
range_explanation: A useful estimate is roughly 0.6 to 3 centimeters per month.
editorial_note: Hair growth varies among people, but scalp hair commonly grows around a centimeter each month.

label: A fast-growing bamboo shoot rising
range_explanation: A useful estimate is up to about 90 centimeters per day.
editorial_note: Only the fastest bamboo species in ideal growth can approach a meter in one day.

label: Jakobshavn Glacier flowing toward the sea
range_explanation: A useful estimate is around 15 kilometers per year.
editorial_note: This unusually fast Greenland glacier has been measured moving many kilometers in a year.

label: A garden snail crawling
range_explanation: A useful estimate is roughly 1 to 10 millimeters per second.
editorial_note: Species, temperature, and surfaces change the result, but a crawling garden snail moves millimeters each second.

label: A raindrop falling through still air
range_explanation: A useful estimate is about 2 to 10 meters per second.
editorial_note: Larger drops fall faster, while wind can change their motion through the sky.
